subject: FastBank EU ingress timeouts & retry amplification — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fastbank.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastbank.com
Date: 2028-06-11T08:12:00Z
Subject: Partial: intermittent 502/504 + client timeouts — EU region

Hi Vivek,

We started seeing a spike of 502/504 errors and client timeouts hitting our EU endpoints around 08:00 UTC. Error rate is currently ~3-5% across our ingress, and a handful of high-value customers are reporting timeouts and failed payments. We've attached a screenshot and a short excerpt of logs showing repeated upstream timeouts.

Impact summary:
- 08:00–08:10 UTC: 502/504 spikes on eu-west-1 front door
- Intermittent 429s observed on some POST endpoints (surge + retries)
- Several customer checkout flows failing (high priority)

Can you confirm:
1) Are you seeing the same on your side?
2) Immediate mitigations you can apply (routing, throttling, backoff)?
3) When can we expect a fix / timeline?

Customers are asking for an ETA and whether logs will be preserved for compliance. Please escalate internally — this is on our exec radar.

Attachments: error_screenshot.png (PNG), logs_excerpt.txt (txt)

Thanks,
Jane
Senior Ops Manager, FastBank
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fastbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Partial: intermittent 502/504 + client timeouts — EU region

Jane — thanks for the heads-up and the artifacts. We're on it. I'm looping in Marcus (eng) and Monica (CS/account) to lead the immediate triage and customer comms.

Immediate actions we are initiating now:
- Opened internal incident INC-2028-1147 and paged Edge SREs
- Short-term mitigation plan: shift some traffic away from the most impacted edge pool, increase upstream timeout to 10s, enable adaptive throttling for non-critical endpoints
- We're preparing a config patch and will push a hotfix if the patch passes a quick safety check (~15 min)

Monica/Marcus — can you confirm whether adaptive throttling + timeout change looks safe for FastBank's config? Marcus, can you attach any quick diffs and the runbook link so I can share ETA with Jane?

Vivek
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T08:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Partial: intermittent 502/504 + client timeouts — EU region

Vivek / Monica — quick findings from the edge telemetry:
- Observed: front-proxy queues in eu-west-1 saturated at ~08:02 UTC; upstream API (payments-kv) latency increased sharply, causing proxy to return 502/504 when backend connection exhausted.
- Retry amplification: client-side retries + aggressive client libraries are increasing concurrent inflight requests, which worsens queueing.

Proposed immediate mitigations (we can implement in the next 10-20 minutes):
1) Increase upstream timeout to 10s (prevents immediate 502s for slightly slower requests)
2) Enable 429 short-circuiting for low-priority POSTs (reject quickly with guidance)
3) Scale additional edge instances in eu-west-1 and add temporary routing weights away from affected nodes
4) Apply a per-customer concurrency cap for FastBank to limit surge (config patch attached)

I've started a canary of the config changes on a small subset of edge nodes. Attaching config_diff.patch. I'll monitor metrics (5xx rate, queue depth, p99 latency) and report back in 10 minutes.

—Marcus
Principal Engineer, Edge Services
Attachment: config_diff.patch
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fastbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T08:55:00Z
Subject: RE: Partial: intermittent 502/504 + client timeouts — EU region

Jane — quick update on what's been done and what to expect in the next 60 minutes: 

Actions completed (08:35–08:50 UTC):
- Increased upstream timeouts to 10s for FastBank routes
- Enabled adaptive throttling for non-critical POST endpoints (low-priority checkout flows will receive 429 rather than exacerbate queueing)
- Scaled eu-west-1 edge pool by +3 instances and reweighted traffic away from the saturated nodes
- Started capturing extended logs and flagged them for retention (we will preserve logs for the RCA)

Short-term impact:
- 5xx rate dropped from ~4.6% to ~0.9% in the impacted pools within ~10 minutes of the change
- You may still see intermittent 429s as we short-circuit low-priority retries — this is intentional to reduce amplification

Next steps:
- Marcus will continue to monitor and run a controlled roll of the config to all EU edges (~45 min)
- We'll prepare a post-incident summary and RCA; I'll include retained logs and a timeline
- Monica will follow up regarding any account-level remedies (credit / SLA) and coordinate exec communications if you want escalation on your side

I've attached a short mitigation_summary.pdf that outlines the steps. Please let me know if we should prioritize additional actions (e.g., full traffic migration to a different region or emergency SLA credit).

—Vivek
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
Attachment: mitigation_summary.pdf
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@fastbank.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastbank.com
Date: 2028-06-11T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Partial: intermittent 502/504 + client timeouts — EU region

Thanks for the fast response and the mitigation steps. We can confirm the error rate on our side is dropping and checkout failures have reduced. A couple of asks: 

- Please confirm logs will be preserved for at least 90 days for our compliance team.
- We need a formal SLA credit quote and an interim executive contact for our CTO — this incident affected high-value customers.
- Can you confirm the timeline for the RCA and whether the config change will be rolled back once things stabilize?

We appreciate the quick action. Monica, Vivek, please keep our CTO (c-level) in the loop if you elevate.

Best,
Jane
Senior Ops Manager, FastBank
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-11T09:25:00Z
Subject: Internal: FastBank escalation — next steps (for records)

Vivek / Marcus — thread recap for internal follow-up: 
- Incident INC-2028-1147 opened; primary mitigations applied and 5xx rate reduced.
- Action items:
  * Marcus: continue monitoring and complete full roll of config to EU (~+45m), run RCA checklist and capture root cause indicators (queue depth, backend p99s, client retry patterns).
  * Vivek: confirm log retention policy (commit to 90 days), prepare external RCA timeline (ETA 48 hours), and draft exec note for customer CTO.
  * Monica (me): begin credit approval workflow with finance and prepare account-facing comms.

I'll escalate to Sales Leadership for credit approval if Jane requests exec escalation. Tagging ENG lead and Finance.

Monica Patel
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference
